CIF_CELL_ANGLE_CORRECTED.condition: A cell angle stored within CIF_ANGLE_CORRECT_MAX_DEG of the value its space group fixes is read as that value. A larger disagreement is not this code: it is refused (ValueError), a judgement under the act.
CIF_CELL_ANGLE_CORRECTED.note: gated by CIF_ANGLE_CORRECT_MAX_DEG (the WP's named tier-3 threshold)

CIF_SITE_TWINS_MERGED.condition: Two atoms of one site closer than TWIN_DISTANCE are read as one, on the special position.

CIF_SITE_LISTED_TWICE.condition: A site whose orbit another listed site repeats, with the same occupancy (and moment) to OCCUPANCY_TOLERANCE and DUPLICATE_U_TOLERANCE, is dropped.

CIF_MAGNETIC_MOMENT_ON_ALLOWED.condition: A site moment off the subspace its site symmetry allows, by less than the file's printed precision, is moved onto it.
CIF_MAGNETIC_MOMENT_ON_ALLOWED.note: gated by magcif.moment_within_print (half a unit in the last printed place, computed per row, no module constant)

CIF_SPECIES_NORMALISED.condition: An atom-type symbol is respelled to the canonical species (case, charge placement, isotope spelling).

SITE_SNAPPED_TO_SPECIAL_POSITION.condition: A site within SITE_TOL (symmetry.py) of a special position is expanded there; cif.py's second site also snaps a site to reach the multiplicity the file states, within CIF_STATED_MULTIPLICITY_SNAP_TOL.

CIF_SITE_MULTIPLICITY_DISAGREES.condition: A stated site multiplicity differs from the one the coordinates give, and no move within CIF_STATED_MULTIPLICITY_SNAP_TOL reconciles them. Nothing is moved; the record says the file disagrees with itself.
CIF_SITE_MULTIPLICITY_DISAGREES.note: threshold CIF_STATED_MULTIPLICITY_SNAP_TOL decides snapped (act) versus this

CIF_MAGNETIC_CENTERING_ASSUMED.condition: A magCIF with no centring loop is read with the trivial centring x,y,z,+1 alone.

CIF_MAGNETIC_NUMBER_MISMATCH.condition: The BNS/UNI numbers a file states disagree with those of its own operators; the operators' numbers are stored and the stated ones dropped. The disagreement is also an assertion that the file is wrong.
CIF_MAGNETIC_NUMBER_MISMATCH.note: act with a judgement inside: which of two statements is right is decided for the operators

CIF_MAGNETIC_NUCLEAR_GROUP.condition: Positions are refined under the nuclear group the file's operators contain, and moments under the magnetic one; recorded which relation held.

CIF_MAGNETIC_NUCLEAR_SETTING.condition: Positions are refined under the file's own group (or its operator list) instead of the parent it names, because the parent's setting does not contain the operators.

MAGNETIC_ION_ASSUMED.condition: A magnetic site states no oxidation state and the neutral table lacks the element: its form factor is taken from an assumed ion (form_factor's assumed-ion table, 2002's B15).
MAGNETIC_ION_ASSUMED.note: the table is the judgement under the act; ruled by 2002 (B15), tiered here after it

LANDE_G_ASSUMED.condition: A site with an assumed ion that needs a g states none: the ion's Hund's-rule g_J is used.
LANDE_G_ASSUMED.note: as MAGNETIC_ION_ASSUMED; both raise sites also in strategy/magnetic.py (2002 tiers them there)

CIF_MAGNETIC_ION_UNCHARGED.condition: A magnetic site states no oxidation state and its label is a bare element: the neutral-atom form factor is used.

CIF_MAGNETIC_MAGNITUDE_ESD_NOT_STORED.condition: A site states moment.magnitude_su; Structure has no field for it, so it is dropped.

CIF_MAGNETIC_SPHERICAL_ESD_NOT_STORED.condition: A moment stated in spherical form carries su values; they are not propagated to the crystal-axis components.

CIF_MAGNETIC_SYMMFORM.condition: A site states symmform; its free-parameter count is compared with the subspace the file's operators give. Level is info when they agree (or the string is unreadable), warning when they differ. No value is changed: the derived subspace is used either way.
CIF_MAGNETIC_SYMMFORM.note: level depends on a comparison the reader makes

CIF_MAGNETIC_UNIDENTIFIED.condition: The operator list does not match one of the 1651 magnetic space groups in spglib's database, so no UNI number is recorded. Reports that a lookup found nothing; no value was changed or chosen.
CIF_MAGNETIC_UNIDENTIFIED.note: unclear: an absence, neither an act nor an assertion about the file

CHILD_GROUP_UNNAMED.condition: magnetic_supercell() found a child group with no tabulated name. States a fact about the result; the group is still carried as operators.
CHILD_GROUP_UNNAMED.note: unclear: an observation about a derived group, not a repair of a file

SPACE_GROUP_SETTING_ASSUMED.condition: A symbol the tables hold in more than one setting is resolved to one of them (the evidence is the composition each setting implies; WP-1118).
SPACE_GROUP_SETTING_ASSUMED.note: act with a judgement inside: which setting is chosen

READER_OPTION_IGNORED.condition: A reader option the chosen format does not take is not applied.

PATTERN_MULTISCAN_DEFAULTED.condition: A file holds several scans and none was named by scan=: scan 0 is read.

PATTERN_SCAN_REVERSED.condition: Points stored from high to low are reversed to ascending.

PATTERN_DUPLICATE_POINTS.condition: Repeated x values carrying the same intensity are dropped.

PATTERN_X_AXIS_ASSUMED.condition: A format whose axis label is absent or unrecognised: the x column is read as 2θ in degrees.
PATTERN_X_AXIS_ASSUMED.note: the alternative is the refusal in the same function for an axis known not to be 2θ

PATTERN_INTENSITY_SCALED.condition: Intensity or σ is not the file's number: the unit is cps with no usable counting time, an unrecognised unit, or values not integral within INTEGRAL_TOL; no σ is supplied (Poisson fallback). Five sites in four readers (base, brml, uxd, xrdml).

BRML_ABSORBER_ENGAGED.condition: A Bruker .brml used an automatic absorber over some points; the stored intensities already include the correction, and this records it.

RAS_ATTENUATOR_PRESENT.condition: A Rigaku .ras carries an attenuator factor other than 1: it is applied (or not) by the measured vendor convention and said so.
RAS_ATTENUATOR_PRESENT.note: the per-format convention is the judgement under the act

XRDML_ATTENUATOR_APPLIED.condition: A PANalytical .xrdml carries a beam attenuation factor over some points: it is applied to the intensities.

GSAS_BANK_COMMENTED.condition: A GSAS file has no live BANK record but a commented one: that one is read.

PATTERN_ROWS_DROPPED.condition: Numeric rows whose column count differs from the file's are not read as data.
PATTERN_ROWS_DROPPED.note: the file's arity is taken from the rows themselves

PATTERN_SIGMA_CONSTANT.condition: The σ column holds one value on every point. Raised after the read, no change made: the reader asserts that such a σ is not a measurement.
PATTERN_SIGMA_CONSTANT.note: asserts a judgement about the file

PATTERN_X_AXIS_IMPLAUSIBLE.condition: The x axis starts at or below 0° with some points at or below 0°, in a format read as 2θ: the reader asserts the axis is not what it was read as. Nothing is changed.
PATTERN_X_AXIS_IMPLAUSIBLE.note: asserts a judgement; TWO_THETA_MAX_DEG is the upper-end refusal elsewhere in readers.py

PATTERN_DEAD_CHANNELS.condition: A run of channels carries a small fraction of the local background with an esd that fell with it: the reader asserts they are dead. Nothing is dropped. The run and window lengths and the fraction are in background.diagnostics.dead_channels, outside io/.

GSAS_FIELD_OVERFLOW.condition: A GSAS record field holds only asterisks (a Fortran overflow): the field is read as absent.

GSAS_PRM_FIELD_DROPPED.condition: A .prm record or field has no slot in the Instrument and is not carried.

GSAS_PRM_PROFILE_SET_DEFAULTED.condition: Bank 1 offers several profile sets and none was named: one is read.

GSAS_PRM_GEOMETRY_ASSUMED.condition: A .prm states no geometry, so none is read from it.

GSAS_PRM_VALUE_NARROWED.condition: A written value needs more characters than a .prm's fixed columns hold and is written to what fits.

GSAS_PRM_FIELD_NOT_WRITTEN.condition: The Instrument holds parts the .prm cannot state; they are not written.

GSAS2_INSTPRM_VALUE_DEFAULTED.condition: An .instprm states no value for some fields: they come back at this package's default.

GSAS2_INSTPRM_CONVENTION_ASSUMED.condition: SH/L (GSAS-II's combined (S+H)/L) is split evenly into axial_sl and axial_hl.
GSAS2_INSTPRM_CONVENTION_ASSUMED.note: an assumption (the even split) under the act

GSAS2_INSTPRM_GEOMETRY_ASSUMED.condition: An .instprm states no Diff-type: the geometry is GSAS-II's own fallback.

GSAS2_INSTPRM_FIELD_NOT_READ.condition: An .instprm states items the Instrument has no place for; they are not read.

GSAS2_INSTPRM_VALUE_MERGED.condition: On writing, axial_sl and axial_hl differ and are written as one SH/L.

GSAS2_INSTPRM_VALUE_FLOORED.condition: On writing, SH/L is below INSTPRM_SHL_FLOOR: it is written as it stands, and GSAS-II floors it when it evaluates.
GSAS2_INSTPRM_VALUE_FLOORED.note: notes the floor INSTPRM_SHL_FLOOR a target program applies

GSAS2_INSTPRM_FIELD_NOT_WRITTEN.condition: On writing, parts of the instrument the .instprm cannot state are omitted.

GSAS_IPARM_PROFILE_DECLINED.condition: A TOF .iparm bank has no PRCF set 1, or states a set other than 1: the profile coefficients are left at zero or the set is not read (set 1 is GSAS's default whatever its function). Two sites.

GSAS_IPARM_PROFILE_READ.condition: A TOF .iparm's PRCF set 1 is read in the order the Technical Manual lists the coefficients; the order is an assumption and the record says so.
GSAS_IPARM_PROFILE_READ.note: the ordering is an assumption under the act

GSAS_IPARM_FIELD_DROPPED.condition: Records and fields with no slot in the schema are not carried.

GSAS2_INSTPRM_FIELD_DROPPED.condition: TOF .instprm items were read and not carried.

GSAS_IPARM_LEGACY_LAYOUT.condition: A LANSCE legacy .iparm: a value running across a BNKPAR boundary is re-read by whitespace tokens (GSAS-II reads it the same way); PRCF set 1 of legacy banks is read as slots 1-8; a non-zero fifth ICOFF pair is carried as written. Three sites.

FULLPROF_MAGNETIC_PHASE_READ.condition: A magnetic phase of a .pcr is read as the moments of its nuclear phase, its SYMM/MSYM pairs becoming a magnetic group.

FULLPROF_MAGNETIC_PHASE_OMITTED.condition: A magnetic phase of a .pcr is not built (not read as moments).

FULLPROF_SPECIES_NORMALISED.condition: A FullProf species is respelled to the canonical species.

FULLPROF_ORIGIN_CHOICE.condition: A space-group symbol with an origin choice is resolved to one; the occupancy-ratio check (_OCCUPANCY_RTOL) accepted it.
FULLPROF_ORIGIN_CHOICE.note: gated by _OCCUPANCY_RTOL; the setting choice is the judgement under the act

FULLPROF_OCCUPANCY_UNCHECKED.condition: The occupancy-ratio check compared a single site with itself, so it passed for a setting without testing it. States that a check that would have decided did not test.
FULLPROF_OCCUPANCY_UNCHECKED.note: asserts that a gate was vacuous

FULLPROF_TIE_DROPPED.condition: A codeword tie in a .pcr is not carried onto the Structure (three sites: the caller asked drop_parameter_ties, a general tie, a cell tie the space group does not make).

FULLPROF_RHOMBOHEDRAL_RESTATED.condition: On writing, a rhombohedral-axes phase is written in hexagonal axes with the scale divided by 9. Raised by crystallography/symmetry.py:rhombohedral_restated_diagnostic.

FULLPROF_SPECIES_WRITTEN_NEUTRAL.condition: On writing X-ray, an ion the X-ray table lacks is written as its neutral atom. Raised by crystallography/scattering.py:written_neutral_diagnostics.

GSAS_EXP_HISTOGRAM_NOT_READ.condition: A histogram of a GSAS .EXP is not read; the text names why.

GSAS_EXP_BACKGROUND_NOT_CARRIED.condition: A fitted GSAS background function's coefficients are on the model, not carried into a Background.

GSAS_EXP_PHASE_MAGNETIC.condition: A magnetic phase of a .EXP: its cell and sites are on the model, no magnetism is built.

GSAS_EXP_SPECIES_NORMALISED.condition: A GSAS species is respelled to the canonical species.

GSAS_EXP_COORDINATES_SYMMETRY_FIXED.condition: Sites carry GSAS's X refine flag but sit on fully fixed special positions: the flag is not honoured.

GSAS_EXP_SCALE_NOT_COMPARABLE.condition: The phase scale is seeded at 1e-3, not the file's histogram scale.
GSAS_EXP_SCALE_NOT_COMPARABLE.note: a convention (the seed) under the act

GSAS_EXP_VALUE_NARROWED.condition: On writing, values needing more than the fixed columns are narrowed.

GSAS_EXP_REFINE_FLAG_MERGED.condition: On writing, a group with some members held and some free is written free.

GSAS_EXP_SPECIES_WRITTEN_NEUTRAL.condition: On writing, an ion the X-ray table lacks is written as its neutral atom (helper in scattering.py).

GSAS2_GPX_SETTING_FROM_OPERATORS.condition: A .gpx names a space group whose setting the project's operators settle differently: the operators' setting is used.

GSAS2_GPX_ITEM_NOT_READ.condition: A .gpx item is not read; the text names it.

GSAS2_GPX_BACKGROUND_NOT_CARRIED.condition: A fitted GSAS-II background's coefficients are on the model, not carried.

GSAS2_GPX_PHASE_MAGNETIC.condition: A magnetic phase of a .gpx is not built, or a nuclear phase carries a magPhases partner; level is warning when magnetic phases exist, info otherwise. Two sites.
GSAS2_GPX_PHASE_MAGNETIC.note: level depends on whether magnetic phases exist

GSAS2_GPX_CONSTRAINT_NOT_CARRIED.condition: A .gpx's constraints are none applied; they are on model.constraints.

GSAS2_GPX_TEXTURE_NOT_CARRIED.condition: A spherical-harmonics texture is not carried, for the reason named; level is a parameter of the helper.

GSAS2_GPX_TEXTURE_CONVERTED.condition: A spherical-harmonics texture is carried with each coefficient multiplied by P_l(0) (and by √2 on n≠0 terms).
GSAS2_GPX_TEXTURE_CONVERTED.note: a convention conversion under the act

GSAS2_GPX_SPECIES_NORMALISED.condition: A GSAS-II species is respelled to the canonical species.

GSAS2_CIF_RHOMBOHEDRAL_RESTATED.condition: On writing a GSAS-II CIF, a rhombohedral-axes phase is restated in hexagonal axes (helper in symmetry.py).

GSAS2_CIF_SPECIES_WRITTEN_NEUTRAL.condition: On writing a GSAS-II CIF, an ion the X-ray table lacks is written neutral (helper in scattering.py).

GSAS2_CIF_DEUTERIUM_AS_D.condition: Deuterium sites are written as D; GSAS-II scatters D at 6.681 fm and rietx at 6.671 fm.
GSAS2_CIF_DEUTERIUM_AS_D.note: records a disagreement between two programs' constants

GSAS2_CIF_SETTING_IN_OPERATORS.condition: The setting is stated in the operators and not in the bare symbol, for an ambiguous group.

GSAS2_CIF_FIELD_NOT_WRITTEN.condition: The phase CIF does not state some fields.

TOPAS_FIRST_RUN_READ.condition: An .inp has #if/#elseif on Run_Number and states more than one run: branches are read as the first run reads them.

TOPAS_SPECIES_NORMALISED.condition: A TOPAS species is respelled to the canonical species.

TOPAS_CELL_COUPLING_DROPPED.condition: A cell tie in a .inp is not carried and the space group does not tie it: the value is copied.

TOPAS_FEATURES_NOT_IMPORTED.condition: Features the file states (or calls without a definition) do not reach the Structure. Two sites.

TOPAS_FEATURE_REFUSED.condition: The file states something to_structure refuses to build without, or is time of flight (issue #193). Two sites.

TOPAS_ORIGIN_TRANSLATED.condition: A space-group symbol with an origin choice is read as the canonical one.

TOPAS_BLOCK_SKIPPED.condition: A block of the .inp is skipped and listed on model.skipped_blocks.

TOPAS_MAGNETIC_GROUP_READ.condition: A magnetic phase's group is read from the file or derived; the text says which.

TOPAS_MOMENT_CONVENTION.condition: mlx, mly, mlz are read as fractional-basis components and stored as crystal-axis μ_B (mlx·|a|, …).

TOPAS_MOMENT_G_HELD.condition: A file that refines the Landé g (mg) is read as holding it.

TOPAS_MOMENT_ION_UNCHARGED.condition: A moment and an uncharged species: the species is read neutral.

TOPAS_MAGNETIC_PART_MERGED.condition: A TOPAS str read as the magnetic half of another is merged into it.

TOPAS_PHASE_TERM_READ.condition: A prm p<n>_<term> is read as phase n's term.

TOPAS_SPECIES_WRITTEN_NEUTRAL.condition: On writing, an ion the X-ray table lacks is written neutral (helper in scattering.py; two call sites).

TOPAS_FIELD_NOT_WRITTEN.condition: On writing, TOPAS computes each phase without a texture, magnetic-only width or extinction the Structure carries.

TOPAS_PHASE_RESTATED_IN_P1.condition: A phase with no mag_space_group in TOPAS is written in P1 with every copy tied.

RECIPE_BOUND_HONOURED.condition: A recipe declares min/max and the refinement applies them.

RECIPE_SCHEMA_UNTESTED.condition: The recipe's schema_version is not one this reader was checked against; asserts the reading is unverified. Nothing is changed.

RECIPE_ZERO_WEIGHT_EXCLUDED.condition: Channels carrying weight 0 become excluded regions (the pdCIF dictionary: weight 0 means not used; #1006's row).
RECIPE_ZERO_WEIGHT_EXCLUDED.note: the pdCIF weight rule is the row #1006 enters

RECIPE_FIT_RANGE_CHANNELS.condition: The fit_range selects some channels on an inclusive mask at both ends.

RECIPE_FIELD_DROPPED.condition: A recipe field has no counterpart or no effect here and is dropped (polarization on a neutron instrument; a constant Lorentzian term at zero; a sub-step background-peak width; refinement_cycles; refinement_algorithm). Five sites.

RECIPE_CONVENTION_ASSUMED.condition: SH/L is split evenly into axial_sl and axial_hl.

RECIPE_DISPERSION_DECLINED.condition: Anomalous scattering is declined and f = f0 is used, for the stated reason.

RECIPE_FLAG_DROPPED.condition: A refine flag is not honoured (Z has no place; a background-peak gamma has no counterpart; LG_eta at its off state holds a coefficient). Three sites.

RECIPE_BACKGROUND_RESEEDED.condition: A recipe's Chebyshev background arrives as a count and a flag, so its values start at zero.

RECIPE_BACKGROUND_PEAK_DEGENERATE.condition: A background peak starts at a FWHM that is broad against the fitted range, so it is a polynomial (asserts degeneracy; no change).

RECIPE_FLAG_TRANSLATED.condition: A (magnitude, eta) pair with the eta flag is translated to two free coefficients.

RECIPE_SCALE_RESEEDED.condition: The recipe's phase scales are re-seeded to match the summed calculated intensity to the data.

RECIPE_ENGINE_DEFAULT_DECLINED.condition: A null magnitude that GSAS-II fills with its own default is not filled: the sample broadening is zero here.

RECIPE_NOTHING_REFINED.condition: No parameter is flagged for refinement; the plan has one stage that frees nothing (asserts the recipe frees nothing).

RECIPE_PLAN_STAGED.condition: The flagged parameters are freed over several stages in the McCusker (1999) turn-on order.
RECIPE_PLAN_STAGED.note: McCusker's order is a citation behind the act

rietx.io.cif.blocks.SCAT_SOURCE_MAX.decides: The longest ``_atom_type_scat_source`` value written, held by test.

rietx.io.cif.numbers.LINE_MAX.decides: The longest record checkCIF reads without its PLAT802 note.

rietx.io.formats.base.HEAD_BYTES.decides: How much of a file a *sniff* may look at.

rietx.io.formats.base.INTEGRAL_TOL.decides: How close to an integer a value must be to count as one.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._MAGIC.decides: The four magic strings, longest first so ``RAW1.01`` is not read as ``RAW `` would be if the test were four bytes for every version.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._V4_SEGMENTS.decides: Where the v4 segment chain begins — the only fixed offset in the format past the preamble's date and time strings.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._RANGE_MARKE.decides: Segment "types" that are not segments: each marks the start of a range.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._SEG_KEYVALU.decides: Segment payload layouts, as offsets from the segment's own start.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._SEG_DRIVE.decides: uint32 flag, char[24] name, 20 skip, float64 position.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._MIN_DATUM.decides: A datum is at least one float32 (4 bytes); anything smaller cannot hold an intensity.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._MAX_RANGES.decides: Runaway guards on numbers a corrupt or misread header can make enormous.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._MAX_HEADER.decides: Runaway guard on a v4 header's size, with _MAX_RANGES.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._V3_SCAN_COD.decides: v3's numeric spelling of the names above.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._V3_HEADER.decides: The v3 file header, before the first range header.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._V3_POINTS.decides: v3 range-header field offsets that this reader reads, relative to its start.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._V3_TWO_THET.decides: Same group as _V3_POINTS: v3 range-header field offsets that this reader reads, relative to its start.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._V3_STEP.decides: Same group as _V3_POINTS: v3 range-header field offsets that this reader reads, relative to its start.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._V3_STEP_TIM.decides: Same group as _V3_POINTS: v3 range-header field offsets that this reader reads, relative to its start.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._V3_SCAN_TYP.decides: Same group as _V3_POINTS: v3 range-header field offsets that this reader reads, relative to its start.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._V3_TEMPERAT.decides: Same group as _V3_POINTS: v3 range-header field offsets that this reader reads, relative to its start.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._V3_WAVELENG.decides: Same group as _V3_POINTS: v3 range-header field offsets that this reader reads, relative to its start.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._V3_VARYING.decides: Same group as _V3_POINTS: v3 range-header field offsets that this reader reads, relative to its start.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._V3_RECORD_L.decides: Same group as _V3_POINTS: v3 range-header field offsets that this reader reads, relative to its start.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._V3_EXTRA_RE.decides: Same group as _V3_POINTS: v3 range-header field offsets that this reader reads, relative to its start.

rietx.io.formats.bruker_raw._V3_MIN_HEAD.decides: the last field read above ends here, so a header shorter than this is not one.

rietx.io.formats.dif._MIN_ROWS.decides: How many reflection rows before it is a peak list rather than a coincidence.

rietx.io.formats.gsas._GSAS_TIME_MAP_SCA.decides: A ``TIME_MAP`` step table is written *before* the bank it feeds, and a long one pushes the first ``BANK`` record past the 4 kB ``head`` window the sniff reads — a real HIPD@LANSCE file (``vnb5053.dat`` from the GSAS distribution's own examples) carries a 71-row ``(10I8)`` table and its first bank sits at byte 6068, so the sniff missed it and the file fell to the ``xy`` catch-all and was refused for the wrong cause; ``TIME_MAP`` in the first 4 kB now triggers one more read up to this bound, and a larger table stays unsniffed.

rietx.io.formats.gsas.TIME_MAP_FIELD_CHA.decides: Width of one field of a ``TIME_MAP`` table record, in characters.

rietx.io.formats.gsas.ESD_FIELD_CHARS.decides: Width of one field of an **ESD** bank's data record, in characters.

rietx.io.formats.peaklist._MIN_ROWS.decides: How many such rows before the head is a profile rather than a coincidence.

rietx.io.formats.philips_rd._DATA_START.decides: The magic at offset 0, and where that version's intensities begin.

rietx.io.formats.philips_rd._ANODE_AT.decides: Offsets of the header fields this reader uses.

rietx.io.formats.philips_rd._MAX_VALUE_A.decides: uint16, equal to max(v) in all 28 real files.

rietx.io.formats.philips_rd._ANODES.decides: The anode code table, from the two descriptions and confirmed on the real files: all 28 read 0, and the kit's own prose independently says a Cu tube.

rietx.io.formats.ras._SPEED_UNIT_SECONDS.decides: ``*MEAS_SCAN_SPEED_UNIT`` → seconds per unit of the speed's denominator.

rietx.io.formats.rasx.MAX_MEMBER_BYTES.decides: How much of any one member may be read.

rietx.io.formats.rasx._SPEED_UNIT_SECOND.decides: ``SpeedUnit`` → seconds per unit of the speed's denominator, the same reading ``.ras`` needs: real files say ``deg/min``, and assuming seconds would make every derived counting time 60× short and every σ wrong by √60.

rietx.io.formats.xy._XYDATA_HEADING_LINE.decides: How many lines an ``XYDATA`` file's heading takes, the keyword line included (the keyword, then five heading lines); the reader skips them before the numbers.

rietx.io.instrument_profile._PRCF_TYPE_3.decides: ``INS n PRCF1 <type> <ncoef> <cutoff>`` — the profile-function type this reader reads.

rietx.io.instrument_profile._PRCF_TYPE_R.decides: Names of the PRCF profile types a .prm reader refuses, for its refusal message.

rietx.io.instrument_profile._PRCF_MAPPED.decides: The type-3 coefficients this reader maps, **named from the one table that holds them** (``CW_PROFILE_COEFFICIENTS``, ``io/projects/gsas.py``) rather than restated here: ``GU GV GW`` and ``LX LY`` onto ``ProfileTCHZ``, ``S/L`` and ``H/L`` onto ``Geometry``, ``GP`` refused unless it is zero. Two readers unpacking one coefficient order from two lists is how they come to disagree, so this one is a slice of the other's.

rietx.io.instrument_profile._BANK_COLUMN.decides: A ``.prm`` record's 12-byte key, by column: ``INS``, a three-column bank number, then the record's own name from column 6. The bank columns are blank on the file-wide records (``BANK``, ``HTYPE``) and carry the bank number on the rest.

rietx.io.instrument_profile._NAME_COLUMN.decides: Same group as _BANK_COLUMNS: A ``.prm`` record's 12-byte key, by column: ``INS``, a three-column bank number, then the record's own name from column 6. The bank columns are blank on the file-wide records (``BANK``, ``HTYPE``) and carry the bank number on the rest.

rietx.io.instrument_profile._PRM_COEFFIC.decides: The ``PRCF`` continuation records are ``4E15.6``, so a coefficient gets fifteen columns where a ``.EXP``'s cell edge gets ten.

rietx.io.instrument_profile._PRM_PER_REC.decides: Same group as _PRM_COEFFICIENT_COLUMNS: The ``PRCF`` continuation records are ``4E15.6``, so a coefficient gets fifteen columns where a ``.EXP``'s cell edge gets ten.

rietx.io.instrument_profile._PRM_COEFFIC.decides: One of those fifteen columns is **reserved as a separator**, so a value is written into fourteen and right-justified into fifteen.

Draws per direction on a pair no certificate settles, when the caller names none (issue #565, decision 3): 12 between two irreps, where 8 % of the cubic pairs that 3 draws called equivalent were refuted by a draw within 12 (0.2 % at 12), and 3 inside one irrep. On the cubic ``P n -3 m:1`` at (0, 0, ½) the raise is what gives the four classes of the known answer rather than two. The 3 within an irrep is not measured the same way (the 8 % was counted on cross-irrep pairs only) and applies only to two *different* directions of one irrep, since the isometry certificate settles the rank-1 copies without a draw; 12 there would cost about 4 min more on the known answer (an estimate, not a measurement).

Same group as CROSS_IRREP_DRAWS: Draws per direction on a pair no certificate settles, when the caller names none (issue #565, decision 3): 12 between two irreps, where 8 % of the cubic pairs that 3 draws called equivalent were refuted by a draw within 12 (0.2 % at 12), and 3 inside one irrep. The 3 within an irrep is not measured the same way (the 8 % was counted on cross-irrep pairs only) and applies only to two *different* directions of one irrep, since the isometry certificate settles the rank-1 copies without a draw; 12 there would cost about 4 min more on the known answer (an estimate, not a measurement).

The isometry certificate's accept bound (issue #565, part 3): the relative congruence residual max_s ‖QᵀG^B_sQ − G^A_s‖_max / max|G^A| and the orthogonality deviation ‖QᵀQ − I‖₂ of the quoted Q must both be at most this.
The full-stack guard of a Farkas certificate (issue #565, part 3, the promise made on #772).

The Farkas certificate's accept floor (issue #565, decision 2): a draw is certified only when the projected dual's optimum, λ_min/|λ|_max of Σ_s y_s G_s on the kernel-projected stack, is at least this.

The projected ratio the quoted certificate is moved inside to: the min-norm point sits on the PSD boundary to rounding (ratios −4e-16 to 2e-16 on the 49 draws), where an exact check can go either way between machines, so the certificate stored and checked is the nearest point toward the interior with at least this ratio (or half the interior anchor's, when that is lower). Two decades above ``FARKAS_FLOOR``; the per-certificate rounding bound (≤ 3.4e-14 measured) is more than three decades below it.

A fit transfer (issue #565, item 6) whose margin μ = λ′/Γ on the target's projected live stack is below this is printed as "proved on the float Gram stack": the cone bound cos(ŷ, I) ≥ μ then sits within a few decades of the rounding allowance ρ, and the step from the float G_s to the exact ones (which no certificate here covers) can be a real share of it. A label, not a gate: the verdict rests on cos < μ − ρ either way. Measured on the 246 fit transfers of the six cubic sets (2026-09-30, both machines): μ 1.7e-9 to 3.5e-4, 14 below this, the largest ρ/μ 0.22.

Stokes 2011 Table 2 orientations, keyed by (system, position, kind); the third tetragonal and hexagonal position takes the [110] two-fold and the mirror normal to [1-10] (Table 2's 422 / 4mm rows).

Same group as _TETRA: Stokes 2011 Table 2 orientations, keyed by (system, position, kind); the third tetragonal and hexagonal position takes the [110] two-fold and the mirror normal to [1-10] (Table 2's 422 / 4mm rows).

rietx.crystallography.symmetry.MAX_HKL_G.decides: Ceiling on the (2h+1)(2k+1)(2l+1) enumeration grid ``generate_reflections`` may allocate: ~30M points is ≈ 1 GB of transient int64, far above any physical powder problem (a 100 Å cell at d_min = 1 Å needs 8.1e6) and far below the PiB-scale grids a collapsed cell implies.

rietx.crystallography.symmetry._ORBIT_CH.decides: transient element budget for the orbit-image stack in ``generate_reflections`` — the hkl loop it replaced was O(1) in memory, so the vectorised form chunks to stay bounded.

rietx.crystallography.symmetry._TRANSLAT.decides: Denominator every space-group translation is an exact multiple of, which is what lets a stated operator be compared with a tabulated one by integers rather than by tolerance.

rietx.crystallography.symmetry.SYMMETRY_.decides: Largest deviation of a symmetry-fixed cell angle from its exact value that :func:`cell_constraints` accepts, in degrees.

rietx.crystallography.symmetry._GAMMA_HE.decides: The exact angle a hexagonal/trigonal γ takes on hexagonal axes.

rietx.crystallography.symmetry.SITE_TOL.decides: Default tolerance, in fractional coordinates, for "this operation fixes this site".

rietx.crystallography.symmetry._COINCIDE.decides: Tolerance at which two images of an *already snapped* position count as the same orbit member.

rietx.crystallography.symmetry._SNAP_NOI.decides: Below this the snap did nothing and ``SiteOrbit.shift`` reports 0.0.

rietx.crystallography.symmetry._SNAP_MES.decides: How many snapped sites a ``SITE_SNAPPED_TO_SPECIAL_POSITION`` message names before it says "and N more".

rietx.crystallography.wyckoff._VOIGT.decides: Index pairs of the symmetric-tensor components in storage order.

reader_decisions.name: io.formats.dif._MIN_ROWS
reader_decisions.decides: Three hkl rows or more make a file a peak list; fewer is refused as a coincidence.

reader_decisions.name: io.formats.peaklist._MIN_ROWS
reader_decisions.decides: Eight rows or more before a head is read as a profile rather than a peak list.

reader_decisions.name: io.formats.gsas._GSAS_TIME_MAP_SCAN_BYTES
reader_decisions.decides: The sniff reads 64 kB, not 4 kB, so a long TIME_MAP table before the first BANK record is still recognised; a larger table falls to the xy reader, refused for the wrong cause.

reader_decisions.name: bruker_raw drive pick (atol=1e-6)
reader_decisions.decides: Which drive record is the scan axis: a flagged drive whose position matches the range start within np.isclose atol 1e-6 deg. A function-level literal, not a module constant, so no walk sees it.

reader_decisions.name: bruker_raw counting-time windows
reader_decisions.where: src/rietx/io/formats/bruker_raw.py:398 (v4: 0 < step_time_ms < 1e9, ms to s) and :572 (v3: 0 < step_time < 1e6)
reader_decisions.decides: Whether a counting time is usable, so whether sigma can be derived by arithmetic or is withheld (Poisson fallback). Two function-level windows.

reader_decisions.name: pdcif weight column
reader_decisions.decides: _pd_proc_ls_weight becomes sigma = 1/sqrt(w) only if every weight is positive; one zero weight drops the whole column and the Poisson fallback applies, with no diagnostic. xy.py:183 and chi.py:90 adopt a third column as sigma when any value is positive.
